name: @insolvia-ai/app
//: The Insolvia app — Expo / React Native, shipped as a web SPA.
A member of the root npm workspace, so `npm ci` at the repo root installs
it and symlinks @insolvia-ai/tokens. There is NO component library and NO
styling library here: bare React Native primitives + StyleSheet.create,
settled by measurement (docs/adr/0004). Adding gluestack, NativeWind,
Unistyles or Tailwind is a regression, not an upgrade.
Expo's FREE tier only: none of the paid EAS services, no EAS config file,
no EAS command-line tool, no Expo access token in CI, and no over-the-air
updates package. Web builds run in GitHub Actions and hosting is the
existing S3 + CloudFront (infra/modules/web_hosting). A CI step greps for
those names, which is why they are described here rather than spelled out.
ios/ and android/ are deliberately absent: `expo prebuild` generates them
//scripts: .github/workflows/app-*.yml — renaming one orphans a required check.
http://localhost:3000 as an EXACT-MATCH Cognito allowed origin; Expo's own
default is 8081, which that origin list would reject.
`build` passes --clear: Metro's transform cache keys on file content and
config, NOT on environment variables, so a staging export followed by a
production export in the same job can otherwise reuse the staging bundle
and ship it as production (EXPO_PUBLIC_INSOLVIA_ENV is inlined at
transform time). The cost is a cold Metro cache per build; the failure it
prevents is shipping the wrong API base URL.
//dependencies: Versions are the ones verified end-to-end in the Expo spike and are pinned
as a set: Expo SDK 57.0.8 / React Native 0.86.0 / React 19.2.3 /
expo-router 57.0.8. Upgrade with `npx expo install --check`, never one
@insolvia-ai/api-client is wired in but not yet imported, exactly as the
Dart client was in the old pubspec.yaml: it sits beside
src/config/environment.ts's apiBaseUrl so the first API-backed feature only
//react-test-renderer: A peer of @testing-library/react-native, pinned to the SAME version as
react. It must be declared: left to npm, the peer resolves to the newest
react-test-renderer, whose own `react` peer is then narrower than our
pinned 19.2.3 and the install fails with ERESOLVE. Bump it in lockstep with
//jest: jest-expo's native preset. Tests assert accessibility PROPS (role,
aria-level, aria-labelledby); that those props become real <h1>/<button>/
<label>-equivalent tags is react-native-web's own mapping, re-verified
against the built DOM in the deploy checks rather than mocked here.
`transformIgnorePatterns` is deliberately NOT overridden. The preset's own
list is what has to win: expo-router 57 pulls in `standard-navigation`,
which ships untransformed ESM and appears only in the preset's list. A
hand-copied list (they circulate widely) silently drops it and every route
test dies with "Cannot use import statement outside a module".
`moduleNameMapper` restates the `@/*` alias from tsconfig.json. Metro reads
the tsconfig paths itself; Jest does not, so without this every `@/`
import fails to resolve under test while building fine.
